subject: Introducer fee and demo-credit attribution workflow for integrator partners
messages:
From: Lila Park <lila@cloudframe.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji@banyanconsult.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: CloudFrame partner proposal + quick ask on attribution

Hi Irene —

Hope you’re well. I’m Lila, partnerships at CloudFrame Integrations (we do systems integration for mid-market fintechs). Kenji (cc) is a consultant who helps us with commercial ops. We spoke at a conference last month and CloudFrame is interested in doing a joint referral + reseller flow for a handful of customers that need on-prem / VPC deployments.

High-level asks:
- Introducer fee for early proofs (one-off finder fee for partner-introduced customers)
- Ongoing revenue share for resale when CloudFrame is the reseller (standard 15–20% target)
- Demo credits to the partner for technical enablement / PoC (approx 8–12 hours of demo/technical support credits per pilot)
- Clear lead registration timeframe and MOP (how far back is a valid lead, handoff requirements)

I attached a short intro deck and a proposed sketch of the flow. Can you point me to the right contact on Redwood’s side for commercial + ops (contracting) so we can scope a starter agreement?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call next week.

Best,
Lila Park
Head of Partnerships | CloudFrame Integrations
partners@cloudframe.io
Attachment: cloudframe-introdeck.pdf (8 pages)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lila Park <lila@cloudframe.io>
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji@banyanconsult.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: CloudFrame partner proposal + quick ask on attribution

Hi Lila —

Thanks for the intro and the deck — excited to explore this. I’ve looped in Ben (partner ops) and Camila (commercial partnerships) to scope commercial terms and lead registration. Quick answers up front:

- Introducer (finder) fee: we can do a short-term, one-off credit for validated introductions that convert to paid deals within 90 days; typical starter is a fixed $5k finder fee or 3% of first-year ARR (whichever is higher).
- Revenue share: we prefer a tiered resale split — starter at 15% for transactional resale, moving to 20% when CloudFrame owns implementation and renewal (T&Cs in MOU).
- Demo credits: we can issue partner demo credits applied as $X of Redwood-hosted usage or as reserved bench time on Dedicated depending on deployment type; we’ll document the mechanism in the playbook.
- Lead registration: require registered lead form, proof of contact, and email thread within 30 days of first outreach; lookback to prior activity capped at 45 days with exceptions for named accounts.

Ben/Camila — can you weigh in on the MOP (minimum operating procedure) and whether the 45-day lookback is feasible? Also flag any compliance or billing constraints for revenue share when the partner is the reseller (tax/invoicing, PoB).

Lila/Kenji — if you’re open, we’ll draft a one-page MOU outlining the above and a sample playbook for credits and lead registration. If that looks good I’ll route to legal for a redline after we confirm numbers.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

(see above)

My comments:
- Introducer fee: OK to offer a $5k flat finder fee for the first pilot (finance prefers fixed for clarity). If the deal is > $250k ARR, we convert to 3% of first-year ARR.
- Revenue share: 15% reseller margin is fine to start. However, if CloudFrame is doing implementation + managed services and we pass through dedicated infra, bump to 20%. Need a clause for trial/demo customers where partner credit is consumed before paying Redwood invoice (credit reconciliation).
- Credits: recommend issuing demo credits as a redeemable voucher code tied to CloudFrame’s partner account that reduces billed usage until exhausted; track via partner account in Console.
- Lead registration: sample-mop.xlsx includes required fields (company, first contact, date, evidence link). We should allow 7 days for internal validation before approving registration.
- Invoicing: prefer Redwood invoices to end-customer with partner-revenue split via partner payout run; however for certain regulated clients partner will invoice and Redwood will pay revenue share. Add tax/PO box options.

Action items:
1) Camila to draft starter MOU language (commercial bullets + 90/45 lookback).
2) Irene to confirm demo-credit mechanism and partner portal tracking requirements.
3) Finance/legal check: Marissa to review invoicing/resale path and required contract templates.

Ben
Head of Partner Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachment: partner_playbook_v1.pdf, sample-mop.xlsx
From: Lila Park <lila@cloudframe.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: CloudFrame partner proposal + quick ask on attribution

Thanks everyone — that all looks straightforward. We’re good to proceed with the MOU + partner playbook approach. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- For the $5k finder fee, can Redwood issue a partner credit within 30 days of first paid invoice? We prefer credits rather than direct check for our ops flow.
- For demo credits as voucher codes — happy with voucher flow. Please confirm expiry window (we’d like 120 days).
- For invoicing, CloudFrame can act as reseller or referral depending on customer preference; if Redwood needs the customer on our books for compliance, we’ll accept referral and split via a payout.

Next step: please send the one-page MOU and playbook link; Kenji and I will review and route to our procurement. If it helps, we can sign a simple MOU and then finalize SOW & resale appendix after the first pilot.

Appreciate the quick turn. Looking forward to the draft.

Best,
Lila Park
Head of Partnerships | CloudFrame Integrations
